newsitem.title: ITALY: Nobel winner Belo says peace depends on U.N.
newsitem.headline: Nobel winner Belo says peace depends on U.N.

text.p: East Timor's Catholic Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, awarded the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday, was quoted as telling his religious order that only the United Nations could bring peace to the former Portuguese colony.

In an interview with the information service of his Rome-based Salesian order, Belo was asked if he had a workable solution to the problem of East Timor, invaded and annexed by Indonesia 20 years ago.
"I have none, he said. "The answer must come from the United Nations because the problem is being handled by them. They have to decide what is best for the people of East Timor."
He said the people had been waiting 20 years for the U.N., which has not acknowledged East Timor's annexation, to find a
"Our role is simply to work for peace and human rights... my work is purely pastoral, in famen, young people and all people," he said, rejecting the notion that his work had a political nature.

Belo won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize jointly with independence activist Jose Ramos-Horta for their efforts to bring peace in the territory of East Timor, which Indonesia invaded after Portuguese colonisers left in 1975.
Since the Indonesian invasion, the Roman Catholic Church has been a refuge for East Timorese coming to terms with the upheavals and trauma of Jakarta's sometimes brutal presence.

"The Pope has always been very close to us. He told me: 'I pray night and day for East Timor.'" Belo said. "The Pope is in full solidariety with the people of Timor."

"As far as the Vatican goes I have to say there has been support and orientation in terms of doctrine and teaching but on the diplomatic front, I can't say the same thing," Belo was quoted as saying after hearing about winning the Nobel prize.
